Subject: Long-context evals recap + next steps

Hi Emily / Ben 

Thanks again for the call today  quick recap and proposed next steps for the long-context evaluation we discussed (summarization fidelity / truncation behavior / model fit).

Summary of the call:
- Goal: measure summarization fidelity and truncation artifacts when feeding 30k	60k token docs into candidate models; verify that Redwood "context-preserving" execution (prefix caching + KV cache) reduces effective truncation loss for multi-pass summarization.
- Primary concerns you raised: (1) summaries losing earlier-page details, (2) cost/latency at 32k+ windows, (3) regression risk when using aggressive quantization.

Recommended models to evaluate (starting point):
- Llama-2-70b-chat (32k variant)  strong instruction-following; baseline for quality.
- Redwood-optimized-30b-q4  good cost/latency tradeoff; run both q4 and int8 if possible.
- Open-Refine-16k (for cheaper per-call fallback when recent context fits).

Initial tests we propose (attached):
1) 1k-sample long-doc summarization suite (attached as long_context_prompt_set_v2.md) run at window sizes: 16k, 32k, 64k (where model supports it). Record truncation-rate metrics and ROUGE/BERTScore vs reference summaries.
2) Truncation stress test: artificially preface doc with low-relevance padding to measure recall of early-section facts after summarization.
3) Quantization regressions: same prompt set on float32 vs q4 vs int8 to flag drift.

Attachments: long_context_prompt_set_v2.md (prompt set), redwood_long_context_eval_v1.csv (initial sample results).

Next steps / owners:
- Dev Patel (SE) to run the 1k-sample suite on the three candidate models and drop results to the Drive folder by Thu Jul 2.
- Redwood to provide per-model latency/cost estimates for 32k/64k windows (Vivek to own).
- Acme to share 100 redacted long-docs (if comfortable) for a final pass  Emily/Ben to confirm sharing method.

Can you confirm this plan and whether Acme wants Redwood to run the initial 1k-sample on your behalf (we can do it in your dev region under a scoped dataset)?

Thanks,
Marissa

On Fri, Jun 26, 2026 at 10:05 AM Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acme.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa  this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before we confirm dataset sharing:
>
> 1) On truncation behavior: do you have a recommended default for how to chunk vs. keep as single long input?

Great questions  answered inline below.

1) Chunking vs single input:
- If the downstream task is a *single* global summary, keeping as a single long input (when model supports the window) preserves ordering and cross-chunk attention, which usually improves fidelity. Where the model cannot fit (or cost is prohibitive), we recommend a hierarchical approach: chunk -> generate section summaries -> synthesize a global summary. Redwood's caching + prefix-merge helps keep the top-k context alive for multi-pass approaches, which reduces loss of early-section facts compared to naive chunking.

2) Quantization delta:
- In our internal evals on summarization suites, we typically see small deltas (0.5	2.0 ROUGE points) float32->q4 for large chat-oriented models, larger deltas when moving to int8 depending on the prompt sensitivity. That said, for some document-fidelity tasks we've seen >5 point deltas if quantization interacts badly with instruction-following head layers  that's why we recommend the regression check (float32 vs q4 vs int8) on your reference set.

3) Cost/latency (ballpark; per-call median):
- Llama-2-70b-chat (32k): ~350ms/token tail-latency, estimated $0.20 / 1k tokens for generation (numbers depend on batching).
- Redwood-optimized-30b-q4 (32k): ~120ms/token, estimated $0.06 / 1k gen tokens.
- At 64k windows, expect 1.5	2x latency overhead depending on KV cache effectiveness. We'll provide precise numbers from a quick run.

Hybrid approach: yes  canary with Llama-2-70b + bulk with 30b-q4 is a defensible plan. We can set up an A/B routing rule and quality thresholds (if summary quality drops below X on the canary sample, route to higher-quality model).

I attached: redwood_recommendations.pdf (short notes + suggested kernel/quant profiles), and dropped the prompt set and the initial eval CSV in the Drive folder.

Action items (updated):
- Dev Patel: run the 1k-sample suite across the three candidate configs (float32 Llama-2-70b 32k, 30b-q4, Open-Refine-16k) and upload results to the Drive folder by 2026-07-02.
- Vivek: compile per-model cost/latency numbers for procurement and include a suggested canary SLA (error budget, rollback threshold).
- Emily/Ben: confirm whether Acme will share redacted doc set, or ask Redwood to run on Redwood-sampled 1k first.

If you're good with this I'll start the scoped dataset access form and loop legal.

Thanks 
Marissa

Vivek / Dev  a quick internal note (copying Emily so she's aware of context):

During the last run on our internal dataset I flagged a consistent pattern: the 30b-q4 variant produced slightly more hallucinations on early-document facts when summarizing >40k tokens compared to float32 Llama-2-70b. The effect looks correlated with the prefix-length and the quantization table we used.

Can we do the following before handing final numbers to Acme?
- Dev: please run the regression check (float32 vs q4 vs int8) on the 100-document subset that Emily is about to share (or our 1k sample if they don't). Focus metrics on factual recall of the first 10% of the doc and an extractive QA pass. Upload the raw CSV and a short note on observed regressions.
- Vivek: draft a recommended canary rollout for Acme: 5% traffic to Llama-2-70b (float32), 95% to 30b-q4; automatic rollback if recall drops >4 pts or if BERTScore delta > 0.03 on the canary sample. Include estimated cost delta.

I'd also like to schedule a 30-min technical review call with Acme next week to walk through the regression methodology and the Drive results. Emily  would Thu Jul 8 at 10am PT work for you?

Thanks 
Marissa
